overview: Two different roles a laboratory test can play, distinguished by the population tested and the purpose of the result.
genZNote: Screening casts a wide net. Diagnostic testing zeroes in on the catch.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: A test applied to a large, typically asymptomatic population to identify individuals at higher risk who need further evaluation.
aspects.valueB: A test applied to symptomatic individuals or those with a positive screen, aimed at confirming or ruling out a specific disease.

aspects.label: Target Population
aspects.valueB: Symptomatic individuals or those already flagged by a screening test.

aspects.label: Test Characteristics Prioritized
aspects.valueA: Prioritizes high sensitivity to avoid missing cases, accepting some false positives.
aspects.valueB: Prioritizes high specificity to confirm true disease and avoid false diagnoses.

aspects.label: Cost and Invasiveness
aspects.valueA: Generally cheaper, faster, and less invasive (suitable for widespread use).
aspects.valueB: Often more expensive, slower, or more invasive, justified by the need for diagnostic certainty.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Mammography for breast cancer screening; PSA test.
aspects.valueB: Breast biopsy to confirm a diagnosis suggested by an abnormal mammogram.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Applied broadly to detect risk in asymptomatic people.
aspects.valueB: Applied narrowly to confirm disease in suspected cases.
